Execution order: Markdown step 3 of 12. Depends on Adashi task ID 26 (Markdown 02/12 — Implement SQLite persistence and guarded document mutations). Complete and verify that prerequisite before starting; all earlier Markdown steps are transitively required.

Implement the same Markdown domain in src-tauri/src/storage/text, using canonical JSON records and the existing multiline representation. Generated .md exports remain derived.
Scope:
- Extend closed collection lists, relational schema materialization, record encoding/decoding, UUID references and API aliases, ordered associations, tombstones, fingerprints, validators, snapshot/commit dispatch and transfer inventories.
- Define and implement any required format/schema upgrade. Existing compatible reads remain byte-stable; unsupported newer formats fail explicitly. Do not rewrite all records on a read or unchanged save.
- Include Markdown in before/after journal publication, rollback/recovery and same-checkout operation receipts. Preserve current separation of Git-tracked canonical data from local request history, machine paths and generated-output ownership state.
- Detect invalid references, conflict markers, identity collisions and stale content even when branch counters match; never silently import generated files or automatically resolve prose merge conflicts.
Acceptance:
- Run the shared contract against text storage, including exact body round trips, no-op/read mtime stability, stale tokens, failed publication and recovery.
- Use independent clone fixtures to verify disjoint documents/edits merge with valid references, overlapping edits remain explicit conflicts, and deletion tombstones do not resurrect documents.
- SQLite and text expose identical visible Markdown identity/content/reference semantics.

Formal design: retrieve the linked owner specifications. The Markdown extension saved on 2026-09-25 is approved design; implementation remains pending until this task is verified.

data.title: Markdown 03/12 — Implement Markdown in Git text storage and recovery
